value.note: States the main theorem: global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions of the three-dimensional relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system for smooth compactly supported data, with no smallness assumption.
value.quote: The formalized result gives global existence and uniqueness for the three-dimensional one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system. The initial particle density is nonnegative, smooth, and compactly supported; the initial fields have bounded derivatives of all orders, finite energy, and satisfy both Gauss constraints. The solution is smooth on every finite time interval, has compact particle phase support there, and is unique among classical solutions. No smallness, symmetry, or neutrality assumption is imposed.

statements.name: thm:global
statements.text:
\label{thm:global}
Every smooth admissible datum \eqref{eq:data} generates a unique global
classical solution of \eqref{eq:rvm}. For every finite $T$, this solution
satisfies
\[
 f\in C^\infty([0,T]\times\R^3_x\times\R^3_v),\qquad
 E,B\in C^\infty([0,T]\times\R^3_x;\R^3),
\]
and $f$ has compact phase-space support on $[0,T]$.
The two divergence constraints hold for all time.
